newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-NEW GENERATION STARTING TO BLOSSOM ON EUROPEAN TOUR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NEW GENERATION STARTING TO BLOSSOM ON EUROPEAN TOUR.

text.p: The European golf tour may not have a budding Tiger Woods to electrify its audiences but there are signs that a new generation is finally beginning to blossom.

For most of two decades the Tour had ridden on the backs of such luminaries as Spaniards Seve Ballesteros and Jose Maria Olazabal, German Bernhard Langer and Britons Nick Faldo, Ian Woosnam, Sandy Lyle and, most recently, Colin Montgomerie.

Age, injury and absence have left Montgomerie alone as a sure-fire European Tour star as he begins his bid for a record-breaking fifth Order of Merit title when the new season opens with the Johnnie Walker Classic in Australia next week.
Woosnam, if his suspect back holds out, and the U.S.-based Faldo, the Masters champion, should join him on the European team to defend the Ryder Cup under the captaincy of Ballesteros in September.
Ballesteros would like to be playing captain but his own form has slipped too much to make that a likely proposition.

Olazabal continues to suffer from rheumatoid arthritis in his feet which has kept him out of the Tour for 18 months and for which he is having treatment in Germany. His return to the tour is still uncertain.

Langer struggled with injuries and putting problems last year, failing to win a full European Tour event for the first time for 17 seasons, although he did capture the Asian Masters after the official season had ended. Lyle stopped being a factor several seasons ago.

So enter the likes of Thomas Bjorn, Padraig Harrington and Raymond Russell, all fresh from excellent rookie seasons, Darren Clarke, Lee Westwood and Andrew Coltart, established players whose talent and dedication could earn them more success and Ryder Cup debuts this year.
Bjorn may turn out to be the best of the lot after an outstanding triumph over a field that included Montgomerie and Faldo at the Loch Lomond Invitational in September.
It made him the first Dane to win a European Tour event and boosted him considerably towards his final position of 10th place on the money list and the prestigious title of rookie of the year.
The tall, powerful Bjorn begins the year second on the Ryder Cup qualifying list from which the top 10 will earn places in the team in September.
Irishman Harrington and Russell, a Scot, both won smaller events against lesser fields early in the year but did well enough overall to finish 11th and 14th on the money list.

Westwood made his mark by winning the Scandinavian Masters in August then, after finishing sixth on the money list, ventured to Japan and captured the Taiheiyo Masters title against an international field.
Clarke's triumph in the German Masters was further evidence of the burly Irishman's talent and he should finally fulfil the predictions of stardom which have been directed at him for a few years.
Coltart, another Scot, is still waiting for his maiden Tour victory but his seventh place finish on the money list testifies to his consistency.

While none of these players is a Woods, the dynamic new darling of the American tour, they all have a degree of potential that augurs well for the future of a Ryder Cup year during which new blood is sorely needed if the trophy is to be successfully defended.
